# fluid

Generated by fluid-design from `fluid.config.json`. Don't edit this folder: change the config
and run `fluid generate`, or change a setting (below), which needs no regenerate.

## The idea

You write every size as drawn in the design. One unit, `--fluid`, is exactly 1px when the
window matches your design frame and grows or shrinks with the window, so the page scales as
one drawing. Each band (phone, tablet, landscape, desktop) scales its own design, and type shrinks more
gently than the layout so it stays readable.

## Set up

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import './fluid/fluid.css';
```

Browser zoom needs one script in `<head>`, before first paint:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { FluidHead } from '@/styles/fluid/integrations/next'
<html><head><FluidHead /></head>…
```

Under a strict CSP, pass a nonce (`<FluidHead nonce={…} />`) or allow
`FLUID_ZOOM_SHA256` (in `runtime/zoom.js`) in `script-src`.

## Which class for what

| You are sizing | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| spacing, sizes, positions | `fluid-p-*`, `fluid-w-*`, `fluid-gap-*`, `fluid-top-*`… | `fluid-py-120` |
| headlines and big numbers: shrinks less than the layout, so it stays readable on small screens | `fluid-display-*` (size/line) | `fluid-display-64/72` |
| body text, labels, button text: shrinks least of all | `fluid-copy-*` (size/line) | `fluid-copy-16/24` |
| a button, chip or icon around copy text | `fluid-copy-h-*`, `-px-*`, `-size-*`… | `fluid-copy-h-56` |
| text inside a box that scales with the layout | `fluid-text-*` | `fluid-text-18/24` |
| the header, nav and footer | `fluid-ui-*` (text, h, px, gap…) | `fluid-ui-h-48` |
| the page wrapper (once per section) | `fluid-container` | |
| a strip that reaches the window edges | `fluid-bleed-x` | a carousel track |
| a tweak for one band below desktop | `fluid-phone:`, `fluid-tablet:`, `fluid-landscape:` (desktop is `lg:`) | `fluid-tablet:fluid-px-32` |
| part of the page that stops scaling | `fluid-grow-until-*`, `fluid-shrink-until-*`, `fluid-off` | `fluid-grow-until-1680` |

Write the number as drawn: `fluid-py-120` is 120px at your design frame's size. Bare numbers
in 0.25 steps work (`fluid-p-37`, `fluid-p-8.5`), anything else in brackets (`fluid-p-[8.3]`).
Not scaled, on purpose: border widths, letter-spacing (use `em`), text measures.

## Tuning

Every number you tune is a CSS variable with a default. Set the ones you want to change in your
own `:root`, next to your tokens. Changes apply live, no regenerate:

```css
:root {
  --fluid-desktop-container-padding: 108; /* wider page margins */
  --fluid-phone-scale-min: 0.8;           /* how small the smallest phones get */
}
```

## The CLI

```bash
npx fluid-design-cli@2 settings          # every setting, its default and what it does
npx fluid-design-cli@2 explain 390x844   # what every unit is at a window size, and where each value came from
npx fluid-design-cli@2 check             # config, generated files and settings; put it in CI
npx fluid-design-cli@2 generate          # after editing fluid.config.json
```

(`fluid init` adds `"fluid": "npx fluid-design-cli@2"` to your package.json scripts, so `npm run fluid -- check` works too.)

## Bands

- **phone**: portrait phones: your phone design frame (default 390 wide).
- **tablet**: 600px and wider: the phone design, scaled up.
- **landscape**: a phone on its side (500px tall or less): the phone design, scaled a bit.
- **desktop**: 1024px and wider: your desktop design frame (default 1440×900).
